record_type_quote: We selected these genetic variants in view of our aim to replicate the PROCARDIS investigators' analysis who selected these out of 11 literature SNPs initially considered.

targets.authors: Broadbent HM, Peden JF, Lorkowski S, Goel A, Ongen H, Green F, Clarke R, Collins R, Franzosi MG, Tognoni G, Seedorf U, Rust S, Eriksson P, Hamsten A, Farrall M, Watkins H, for PROCARDIS consortium
targets.title: Susceptibility to coronary artery disease and diabetes is encoded by distinct, tightly linked SNPs in the ANRIL locus on chromosome 9p
targets.evidence_quote: The PROCARDIS Consortium's results showed that two different SNPs, rs2891168 and rs10811661, both in the 9p21 region although rs2891168 belongs to the CAD-associated locus while rs10811661 is localized outside, are associated with CAD and diabetes respectively, and the two susceptibility effects are independent [ 15 ]. However, there are several reasons why the PROCARDIS results cannot be regarded as conclusive. Most importantly, the study was not conceived, and did not have sufficient statistical power to answer this question as the number of diabetic patients without CAD was quite small. To confirm and replicate these results, a larger sample was deemed necessary.
targets.outcome_quote: Our replication study showed that rs2891168 and rs10811661 are independently associated respectively with MI and T2D in an Italian population.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors conclude that the independent susceptibility associations were replicated in their Italian sample; PROCARDIS is the explicitly designated target, rather than earlier GWAS cited as background.

reasoning: Independent Italian case-control sample explicitly re-tests the PROCARDIS findings. One targeted original paper.
